verdicts.mechanism: Kripto byte-pariteliği: IdentitySeam (+16 B) vs gerçek noise-wire
verdicts.claim: Real wire is +26 B/datagram (OUTER_HDR_LEN 10 + TAG_LEN 16), so IdentitySeam under-counts Kama by 10 B/pkt; ~15 KB (~12%) on kp-static-r4
verdicts.corrected_value: The +10 B figure picks one of two live envelopes. kama-noise-wire ships BOTH: extended outer = 26 B (schema EXTENDED_OUTER_OVERHEAD = 26) and legacy SESSION_DATA = 22 B (LEGACY_SESSION_DATA_OVERHEAD = 22), and legacy.rs's own header calls the 22 B form the ACTIVE ccr §35.6/§35.9 format. The normative §13 Layer Accounting table gives SESSION_DATA hot-path UDP-payload overhead as 22 B. So the honest under-count is a RANGE of +6..+10 B/datagram, and by the spec's own normative table it is +6 B. The arithmetic the finding does (1496 pkt x 10 B = 14 960 B = 12.2% of 122 377) is correct for the 10 B branch; the 6 B branch gives 8 976 B = 7.3%.

missed_mechanisms.name: Wall-clock budget asymmetry: quinn gets a full max_deadline for handshake AND a full per-message deadline afterwards
missed_mechanisms.evidence: crates/bench/src/quic.rs:252 `let conn = match timeout(cfg.max_deadline, connecting).await {` — the handshake is allowed up to max_deadline. Only after it succeeds does quic.rs:319 `let start = Instant::now();` begin the clock, and quic.rs:331-334 then grants each message `cfg.max_deadline.saturating_add(remaining submission time)`. kama-product has no such pre-phase: crates/bench/src/kama_product.rs:505-509 computes `total_deadline_ns = t0 + (n-1)*interval + max_deadline` from t0. At product_vs_quinn.sh's DEADLINE=30 this lets a quinn run consume up to ~30 s of establishment plus ~35 s of measurement, inside the script's `timeout $((DEADLINE + 40))` = 70 s wrapper (scripts/netem/product_vs_quinn.sh:45). The setup-cost finding names only the BYTE asymmetry; this time asymmetry is larger and cuts the same way (in quinn's favour under §4.4.3 ④, which is precisely the metric that is supposed to punish QUIC's handshake).

corrected_classifications.mechanism: CLUSTER-WIDE CONVENTION (Q-STREAM, Q-DGRAM-ARQ, MTU pins, delivery definition, submit-interval, t0 gates, budget governor, wire accounting, deadline semantics)
corrected_classifications.reason: Under the stated rubric SHIP requires 'implemented + wired into product + required for v1 + exercised', and the DEFINITIONS explicitly say bench is NOT product. Every one of these mechanisms self-declares product_reachable=false or lives entirely in crates/bench. The findings therefore apply SHIP with a silently redefined predicate ('required by the §4.4 benchmark gate' instead of 'wired into the product runtime'). That may well be the right predicate for a bench-harness cluster, but it must be declared, because as written the cluster reports nine SHIP verdicts for code that by the audit's own definition cannot ship in the product. I am not claiming these arms should be deleted — I am flagging that the classification axis was changed without saying so, which makes the cluster non-comparable with the product-side clusters. Recommended fix: keep the substance, relabel the axis (e.g. HARNESS-REQUIRED / HARNESS-GAP / HARNESS-DEAD), or state the redefinition once at the cluster head.

DELETE is not defensible under the given rubric. DELETE means dead/duplicate/obsolete/misleading, but this arm is (a) live-wired into the ADR-18 mandatory nightly gate (.github/workflows/nightly.yml:132 -> harness/run-kama-matrix.sh:20/33), (b) the pre-registered manifest's two Kama arms (scripts/netem/kapi_manifest.py:100-103), and (c) hard-coded as the analyzer's PRIMARY_KAMA (scripts/netem/kapi_analyze.py:22). It is neither dead nor removable without breaking the only quality gate the repo has. It also fails KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL, which requires 'not secretly needed for v1 claims' — it IS the source of docs/results/kama-vs-quinn-v1.md. The honest classification for the defect the finding actually identified is WIRE against the GATE, not DELETE against the arm: §4.4 / ADR-18 require the benchmark to measure the product transport, and the gate is connected to a non-product surrogate (crates/bench/src/kama.rs:7-8 makes FEC structurally unemittable). The v1-blocking work item is 'move the manifest, run-kama-matrix.sh and kapi_analyze.py PRIMARY_KAMA to kama-product'; after that move, and only then, the stub becomes KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL as a crypto-free control arm. The finding's own notes reach this conclusion but the classification field contradicts them.

corrected_classifications.mechanism: Ürün-default sapması #3: fec_loss_risk (bounded_v1 unreachable from bench)
corrected_classifications.reason: WIRE requires 'spec-required + disconnected'. The mechanism is neither disconnected nor incomplete in the product: crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:204 sets `fec_loss_risk: FecLossRiskConfig::bounded_v1()` in RuntimeConfig::default(), and runtime.rs:843 `session.sender_mut().set_fec_loss_risk(cfg.fec_loss_risk)` is a real product hop into the arbiter's speculative lane. It is product-wired and default-on, i.e. SHIP. What the finding actually establishes — and establishes correctly, with a clean negative grep — is a HARNESS-FIDELITY defect: the shipped configuration is not the one any bench arm constructs. Classifying it WIRE mislabels a measurement gap as a v1 product-wiring blocker, which would wrongly imply the FEC v1 closure decision is unimplemented. Correct framing: mechanism SHIP; separately-recorded bench defect 'bench cannot instantiate the shipped speculative policy without five manual flags'.

Same rubric error as #3. Both fields are product-wired and product-default-on: runtime.rs:195 `initial_window_bytes: DEFAULT_BURST_CAP` -> runtime.rs:856 `set_initial_window(...)`; runtime.rs:206 `structure_gate_level_permille: Some(250)` -> runtime.rs:847 `set_structure_gate_level(...)` -> sender.rs:4433 `gate_level_permille()`. Neither is disconnected, so neither is WIRE. The defect is that crates/bench/src/kama_product.rs:161 and :224 write CLI defaults (0 / None) straight over them, so the benchmark measures a configuration the product does not ship — a harness defect, not an architecture gap. For #2 there is an additional mitigating fact the finding notes but does not weight: the deviation is behaviourally inert wherever FEC actuation is Manual (sender.rs:4606), which is every FEC arm in product_vs_quinn.sh, so #2 has had no effect on any published product-vs-quinn number. #1 is the materially damaging one and is fully confirmed.

Classification upheld — this is the one mechanism in the cluster where SHIP is defensible on the literal rubric, since the chain runs through crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs into adaptive_transport and reaches the wire (independently confirmed at kama_product.rs:397/419 -> runtime.rs:843-869 -> seal_send at runtime.rs:925-953, with wire-level corroboration in reports/product-vs-quinn-v3/iid50/kp-static-r4/rep1/out.jsonl `tx.fec=22816`). I am recording it only to correct the stated field count (14 explicitly-set fields, not 12) and the deviation count (five fields can deviate from product default, not three: the three named plus drain_cap and max_unit_bytes).
